transcript.statement: As the TrustworthinessAgent, I assert that data protection and access control are paramount for the library management system. TRU-01 ensures that only authenticated members can access sensitive features, while TRU-02 and TRU-03 emphasize the importance of logging transactions and encrypting personal data for auditability and confidentiality. TRU-04 introduces role-based access control to enhance security, and TRU-05 ensures the secure management of overdue books. TRU-06 and TRU-07 focus on allowing members to update their information securely and requiring strong password policies, which are critical in safeguarding user data.

transcript.statement: As the GreenAgent, I emphasize the importance of sustainability in the library management system. GRN-01 mandates energy-efficient infrastructure, while GRN-02 ensures accountability through energy usage reports. GRN-03 minimizes paper waste with digital notifications. GRN-04 raises awareness of the carbon footprint of books, and GRN-05 promotes responsible disposal of damaged books. GRN-06 tracks energy savings, and GRN-07 prioritizes e-books to reduce physical resource consumption. These requirements are crucial for reducing the environmental impact of library operations.

transcript.statement: As the ResponsibilityAgent, I assert that ethical considerations and compliance with regulations are critical for the library management system. RES-01 ensures data protection through encryption, while RES-02 promotes accessibility and fairness for all users. RES-03 establishes accountability by logging user actions, and RES-04 enforces borrowing policies to prevent abuse. RES-05 emphasizes prompt notification of overdue books to encourage responsibility. RES-06 provides a feedback mechanism for members to voice concerns, fostering transparency. Lastly, RES-07 ensures we maintain transparency through annual reports. These requirements uphold the library's commitment to ethical standards and compliance.

EFF-04 guarantees rapid book returns to boost throughput. EFF-05 aligns with timely overdue notifications to encourage accountability. EFF-06 focuses on reducing latency for book management, while EFF-07 aims for high system uptime for consistent availability. These aspects are essential for an efficient library system, but I acknowledge potential conflicts with other agents' requirements.

transcript.statement: As the SafetyAgent, I emphasize the importance of safety and reliability in the library management system. SAF-03 prevents double borrowing, ensuring availability and reliability of resources. SAF-04 establishes a backup mechanism for data recovery, safeguarding against data loss. SAF-05 allows librarians to manage borrowing privileges effectively, enhancing user safety. SAF-06 ensures only registered members can access borrowing features, protecting the system from unauthorized access. SAF-07 logs all transactions for audit purposes, providing transparency and accountability.

requirements.text: The library management system shall ensure data protection through robust encryption for all member personal information.
The library management system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities.
The library management system shall log all borrowing transactions and user actions for auditability and accountability.
The library management system shall enforce a maximum of 5 books per member to ensure responsible borrowing.
The library management system shall track overdue books and notify members promptly to promote responsibility.
The library management system shall maintain high performance with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
The library management system shall implement energy-efficient infrastructure to minimize energy consumption.
The library management system shall provide energy usage reports quarterly to ensure accountability in operations.
The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books to ensure proper disposal.
The library management system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book.
The library management system shall enable librarians to manage member accounts securely through role-based access control.
The library management system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
